name: Monthly and weekly mine plan
summary: Each month a mine planning engineer works out which development headings, stopes and backfill the underground crews will work next month so that the mine sends enough tonnes and ounces to the mill, using last month's reconciliation, the budget, stope and fill status from the mine captains, equipment availability from maintenance and grades from geology. The draft goes through a geotechnical check, a ventilation check and a planning meeting, is accepted by the mine superintendent and the general manager, and is issued with weekly targets that are re-planned every week. The plan is built in AutoCAD and spreadsheets by one or two engineers on rotation, and late stope releases, equipment breakdowns and reconciliation surprises force mid-month revisions.

baseline.org_archetype: A single-mine Canadian gold producer running a 500-650 tpd narrow-vein underground mine in northern Ontario, with a technical services department of about 20 engineers, surveyors and geologists on a 14-on, 14-off rotation.
baseline.notes: Practice follows the Eagle River mine technical reports (2016, 2022) and the neighbouring Island Gold report (2020); software is AutoCAD with Promine, Microsoft Access drillhole database, Excel workbooks and email, with Deswik and Leapfrog arriving in 2021.

trigger: The mine-to-mill reconciliation and month-end actuals for the previous month are issued, which opens planning for the month after the current one.
end_state: The monthly plan and weekly targets have been issued and executed, with any mid-month revision reissued, and month-end compliance to plan has been reviewed.

volume.seasonality: One plan every month; the December and January plans carry the annual budget changeover and the summer plans carry vacation coverage.

evidence.note: Monthly plan with weekly plans inside it (fowke).

systems.name: Mine design and scheduling software (3D design, scheduling)
Shift reports, line-up boards and production tallies (paper and spreadsheets)
Maintenance management system (ERP maintenance module or standalone)
Shared drives and document library (procedures, permits, drawings)

resources.name: Underground utility fleet (scissor lifts and light vehicles)

steps.name: Collect the reconciliation and month-end actuals
steps.description: The planning engineer saves the reconciliation report, the month-end development metres and stope tonnes from the shift tallies and the survey as-builts, and lists how far each heading and stope got against last month's plan. This shows what carries over into the next plan.

evidence.note: Use of last month's results to set the next plan is named in the organisation file; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Update as-built headings and mined-out stopes
steps.description: The engineer updates the AutoCAD and Promine planning file with month-end face positions, mined-out and filled stopes and new survey lines, so the plan starts from where the mine really is. Metres to go and stope tonnes remaining are recalculated.

error.defect_description: A month-end face position is entered wrong, so metres to go are wrong.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Drive underground to the active workplaces
steps.description: The engineer rides a light vehicle down the ramp to walk the headings, stope brows and fill horizons that will be in next month's plan. The trip waits for a free vehicle and a day when the engineer is not tied up in meetings.

evidence.note: Underground inspection by planners is common practice; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Inspect headings, stope brows and fill status
steps.description: Underground, the engineer checks the face positions, ground conditions, services and the state of open stopes and fill, and notes where the plan must allow for rehabilitation, extra support or waiting for fill to cure. Entry follows the tag board and workplace examination rules.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854: underground entry with tag board, self-rescuer and workplace examination before entering a heading

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Get stope, fill and crew status from the mine captain
steps.description: The engineer asks the mine captain which stopes will finish drilling, blasting and mucking this month, which are waiting for fill, how many development and production crews will be available and which headings have ground or water problems. The captain answers between shifts.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Get equipment availability and planned shutdowns
steps.description: The maintenance planner sends the jumbo, LHD, truck and longhole drill rebuilds and planned services for next month, and the hoist and crusher shutdowns, from the maintenance system. The planner works office hours, so a request sent on a weekend waits.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Supply grades and tonnes for planned stopes and headings
steps.description: The mine geologist gives diluted tonnes and grade for each stope and ore heading in the draft list from the latest grade control outline and stope designs. Where face assays are only a few days old, the figures can still change.

error.defect_description: Stale or uncapped chip grades are used, overstating stope grade.

evidence.note: Grades come from chip samples and the grade control model; chip grades run higher than core (er2022). Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Look up budget and life-of-mine targets
steps.description: The engineer reads next month's budget tonnes, grade, ounces and development metres and the year-to-date variance, and the life-of-mine sequence the month must stay on.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: List available workplaces and set the sequence
steps.description: The engineer lists every heading and stope that can be worked next month, with its constraints (ground support, fill curing, ventilation, shared haulage levels), and sets the order so people, equipment and space do not clash. This list is the backbone of the plan.

evidence.note: The monthly plan aligns people, equipment, materials, time and space (fowke).

steps.name: Schedule development metres by heading and crew
steps.description: The engineer assigns rounds per shift to each development crew and heading, using advance rates for captive sub-levels, mechanised sub-levels and ramps, and totals the metres and ore development tonnes by week.

error.defect_description: Advance rates are optimistic, so planned metres are not reached.

evidence.note: Development drives access to ore and sets output (er2022); weekly and daily planning mostly in spreadsheets (fowke).

steps.name: Schedule stope tonnes, grade and backfill
steps.description: The engineer schedules blasts and mucking by stope (shrink mucking until the last blast, then pulling the stope empty), backfill pours and fill curing, and checks the total against hoisting with 4 t skips, the 30 t underground trucks, the 16.6 km surface haul and the mill's daily feed.

evidence.note: Shrink mucking, skip payload, truck class and surface haul distance (er2022). Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Check airflow against the diesel fleet by level
steps.description: The engineer allocates LHDs and trucks by level and checks that each level gets at least 0.06 cubic metres per second of air for each kilowatt of diesel equipment working there, moving equipment or headings where it does not.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s.183.1(3): at least 0.06 m3/s of air per kW of diesel equipment operating in the workplace

evidence.note: Ventilation rule of Regulation 854 section 183.1(3) quoted in er2022.

steps.name: Geotechnical review of the sequence
steps.description: The geotechnical engineer reviews the stope sequence, pillars and the time open spans will stand before fill, and asks for changes where the sequence leaves a long open span or mines toward a stressed pillar.

control.basis: Site ground control program: geotechnical review of the stoping sequence

evidence.note: Uncemented fill leaves large open spans until the stope is mucked out (er2022); review share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Compare plan physicals with budget
steps.description: The engineer totals planned tonnes, grade, ounces and metres for the month and compares them with budget. If ounces fall short by more than the site's tolerance, the engineer re-sequences to bring forward higher-grade stopes or headings.

evidence.note: Re-sequencing share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Draft next month's definition drill program
steps.description: The chief geologist picks the definition drill holes needed ahead of the stopes in the plan, sets the drill bays and metres for the contract underground rigs and sends the program to the drilling contractor.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Draft the underground services plan
steps.description: The engineer lists the pipe, ventilation tubing, electrical, pumps and refuge work needed for the new headings and stopes and sends it to the services crew supervisor.

evidence.note: The Mishi open pit operated intermittently until early 2021 (er2022); share of months with pit mining is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Draft the open pit plan with the contractor
steps.description: In months when the Mishi pit is mined, the engineer sets the benches, ore and waste tonnes and blast schedule with the open pit supervisor and the mining contractor, and checks the mill blend of pit and underground ore.

evidence.note: Mishi grade control on blast holes and pit operation until early 2021 (er2016, er2022).

steps.name: Run the monthly planning meeting
steps.description: The technical services manager chairs the meeting with the mine superintendent, captains, chief geologist, maintenance and mill, walks through the plan and its risks and records requested changes. The meeting is held on a fixed day late in the month.

evidence.note: Monthly plan reviewed to escalate deviations (fowke); meeting format and change share are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Mine superintendent accepts the targets
steps.description: The mine superintendent confirms operations will commit to the tonnes, metres and crew allocation, sometimes after trimming targets for headings the captains doubt.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: General manager approves the monthly forecast
steps.description: The general manager signs off the month's ounces and cost forecast that goes to the chief operating officer and corporate reporting.

control.basis: Site delegation of authority: monthly production forecast approved by the general manager before reporting to corporate

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Issue the monthly plan package
steps.description: The engineer publishes the plan drawings by level, the heading and stope target tables and the forecast to shift control, maintenance, the mill, ventilation and stope design, and posts the targets on the line-up board.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Set weekly targets and the first week's schedule
steps.description: Before the month starts the engineer splits the targets into weeks and writes the first week's schedule by crew and heading in a spreadsheet, with a look-ahead to the second week.

evidence.note: Weekly plans of one week plus one week look-ahead, mostly in spreadsheets (fowke).

steps.name: Run the weekly schedule reviews through the month
steps.description: Each week the engineer compares actual metres and tonnes with the weekly schedule, meets the captains and maintenance, and reissues the next week's schedule. The time shown is the sum of the three to four weekly reviews after the first week.

evidence.note: Variance to plan reviewed each cycle and compliance tracked weekly (fowke); times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Decide whether a mid-month revision is needed
steps.description: The technical services manager looks at the gap to plan halfway through the month and decides whether to reissue the plan formally, for example when a stope release is late, a jumbo or the hoist is down, or the reconciliation shows a grade shortfall.

evidence.note: Revision share is the author's estimate of the frequent revisions the organisation file describes.

steps.name: Re-sequence and reissue the revised plan
steps.description: The engineer re-sequences the rest of the month around the missing stope or equipment, recalculates the physicals and forecast, and reissues the plan and weekly schedule with the changes marked.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Review compliance to plan at month end
steps.description: After the month closes the engineer compares actual metres and tonnes by heading and stope with the plan, records the reason for each miss and passes the list to the next month's planning and the reconciliation.

evidence.note: Compliance to plan documented monthly from metres completed (fowke).

exceptions.name: Mid-month revision
exceptions.description: A late stope release, a major breakdown or a reconciliation surprise forces a formal reissue of the plan.

exceptions.name: Short of budget
exceptions.description: The first draft misses budget ounces and the sequence is rebuilt.

exceptions.name: Changes at the planning meeting
exceptions.description: Operations, geology or maintenance ask for changes and the stope schedule is redone.

exceptions.name: Open pit active
exceptions.description: In 2019-2020 months the plan also covers the contractor-run Mishi pit.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from reconciliation issued (about day 12 of the month before) to month-end compliance review
benchmarks.population: Monthly underground plan at a small mine

evidence.note: About 16 days to draft and approve the plan before the month, the 30-day month and 2-3 days to review compliance; author's estimate built on the monthly and weekly horizons in fowke.

benchmarks.value: monthly 1+2 months; weekly 1+1 weeks; daily 12+12 hours
benchmarks.population: Oyu Tolgoi underground (large block cave, used for structure only)

pain_points.description: The plan is rebuilt by hand in AutoCAD and spreadsheets each month, and the reference mine's technical report recommends evaluating better short-term planning tools.

evidence.note: er2022 recommends evaluating tools for short-term mine planning and scheduling.

pain_points.description: Stope releases arrive late and reconciliation surprises change grades, forcing mid-month revisions.

evidence.note: Named in the organisation file; frequency is the author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Inputs from captains, maintenance and geology arrive at different times from people on different rotations, stretching the drafting phase.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Output depends on how many headings and stopes can be developed and produced at once, so a few late headings move the whole month.

evidence.note: Gold output relates to the number of mining fronts that can be developed and produced at a time (er2022, er2016).

assumptions: One case covers drafting next month's plan and running it through that month, so cases overlap: the plan for month M+1 is drafted while month M runs.
The weekly reviews after the first week are one aggregated step (s23); its touch time is the sum of three to four weekly cycles.

The mine geologist, mine captain, maintenance planner, geotechnical engineer and general manager take part, although the organisation file's process entry lists only the engineer, manager, superintendent and chief geologist.
Extra interfaces beyond the organisation file: grade control model, maintenance schedule and shift reports as inputs, and the plan sent to reconciliation for planned-versus-actual comparison.
Steps s05-s07 run in parallel in practice; their waits are kept short so the simulated cycle is not inflated.
The wait before s26 covers the rest of the month after the weekly reviews plus two to three days for month-end data, so the case spans about seven weeks.
Loaded costs per hour are taken from the organisation file.

sources.title: Technical Report for the Eagle River Gold Mining Complex, Ontario, Canada (CAPR001445)
sources.publisher: SRK Consulting (Canada) Inc. for Wesdome Gold Mines Ltd.
sources.supports: Reference mine practice: channel (chip) sampling of underground faces by production geologist and technician after each advance once the heading is inspected and supported, sample lengths 0.3 m minimum in ore and 0.3 m maximum with visible gold; test-hole, long-hole and muck sampling (one muck sample per 25-30 t truck, taken by muckers); samples brought to surface at end of the beat geologist's shift and shuttled daily to the company assay office in Wawa; mine lab not accredited, 11% QC insertion (blank, CRM, duplicate per 28-sample tray), VG protocol, low-grade CRM bias; channel results recorded in Promine; polygonal estimates before 2021, Leapfrog/Datamine 3D model from 2021; chip samples average higher than core; mine-to-mill reconciliation within 5%; stope design with 1.5 m minimum width, 0.5 m HW and FW dilution from CMS reconciliation, 90% stope and 99% development recovery, stope cut-off 5.5 g/t, development cut-off 2.0 g/t, density 2.7 t/m3; captive sub-level open stoping via Alimak raises, 13-18 m 64 mm down-holes on a 3-2-3 pattern, shrink mucking, CRF sill mats and URF fill; 19% of mill feed from sill development; ore hoisted in 4 t skips and trucked 16.6 km from the portal pad to the mill; two 12 h shifts 365 days a year; UG labour table with 9 mine engineering and 10 mine geology staff; recommendation to evaluate tools for short-term planning; ventilation rule 0.06 m3/s per kW of diesel

sources.title: Overview of mine scheduling for Oyu Tolgoi Underground Project (Caving 2018)
sources.publisher: Australian Centre for Geomechanics (S. Fowke and B. Groeneveld, Rio Tinto)
sources.supports: Planning horizons: monthly plan of 1 month plus 2 months look-ahead to align people, equipment, materials, time and space and escalate deviations; weekly plan of 1 week plus 1 week; daily shift plan; monthly plans handed to short-range planners for weekly plans; weekly and daily planning mainly in Microsoft Excel; variance to plan reviewed each cycle and compliance to plan tracked weekly, monthly and quarterly

sources.title: Technical Report for the Eagle River Mining Complex including the Eagle River Gold Mine, the Mishi Gold Mine and Related Infrastructure
sources.publisher: Wesdome Gold Mines Ltd. (G. Mannard and P. Ng), hosted by minedocs.com
sources.supports: Chip samples taken every round (every 3 to 4 m) in ore development headings across the full face, about 2.5 kg, 0.3-0.5 m lengths; raises sometimes chip sampled and always muck sampled; muck sample per 25-30 t; sealed samples transported daily to the company Mine Assay office with results emailed to the mine; assay data in Microsoft Access linked to Promine and Surpac/Gemcom, databases updated weekly and audited monthly; about 30% of production from silling and development; CMS surveys show about 1.0 m wall overbreak; Mishi grade control on blast hole samples
